explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. `transport` is a definition in the library itself: it is `L.mapIso` of the path class viewed as an isomorphism, turned into a linear equivalence. `LocalCoefficientSystem` is also the library's own abbreviation for a functor `FundamentalGroupoid X ⥤ ModuleCat R`. The theorem says that transport along the constant path is the identity. That is just the functor identity law (`Functor.map_id`) applied to these definitions, combined with `FundamentalGroupoid.id_eq_path_refl`. Generic functor laws applied to the library's own definitions do not count as a Mathlib duplicate. Mathlib has no notion of local coefficient systems or of this transport map, so there is no Mathlib statement to match.
